title: Always-on agents run production without the on-call tax — Justin Smith, Resolve AI

primary.label: Agent Architecture & Harnesses
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 64%).

domains.label: Enterprise Operations
domains.rationale: The agents handle internal enterprise operations: on-call duty, deployment monitoring, incident triage, operational reports, and handoffs.

domains.label: Developer Platforms
domains.rationale: The tools are designed for software engineers and integrate into development workflows via MCP servers and bring-your-own-skills.

summary: Justin Smith, Founding Product Engineer at Resolve AI, presents the company's background agents — always-on AI agents that autonomously handle production operations, reducing the on-call tax created by AI-accelerated shipping velocity. He frames the problem: 70% of engineer time goes to running code in production rather than writing it, and AI coding tools have widened this gap. Background agents are defined by three principles — when they run, how they run, and how they know what to do — and operate in cloud sandboxes independent of developer machines. Smith demonstrates four workloads: deployment monitoring with dynamic check plans that follow causal chains through production dependencies, scheduled health checks, operational reports and on-call handoffs, and passive Slack question response with confidence gating that decides whether to answer publicly, ask for confirmation via DM, or stay silent. Agent timing is autonomous — an agent may decide to recheck in an hour or return in three days based on the failure class. A learning system captures environment knowledge, which Smith identifies as essential since models alone are insufficient without deep understanding of the production environment. Agents are configured through natural conversation and are accessible via MCP servers for composable integration into existing internal agent harnesses. The talk concludes that the cost of operational work lies in environment complexity, not task execution.
whyItMatters: The software engineering and AI concepts in this talk form a tight loop: the SE concepts (on-call friction, CI/CD gaps, production context as the hard problem) define the operational pain points that motivate the AI concepts, while the AI concepts (background agents, dynamic check plans, autonomous timing, confidence gating, learning systems) are the proposed solution architecture. The bridge between them is the insight that production context — not execution — is where engineering cost lives, which is why a learning system is the critical AI component. The SE infrastructure decisions (cloud sandboxes, Slack as interaction surface, MCP composable integration) are the deployment substrate that makes the AI agents practically useful in real enterprise environments. Without understanding the SE problem space (on-call gaps, unmonitored feature flags, causal chain complexity in production), the AI agent architecture would be solving the wrong problem; without the AI capabilities (causal chain reasoning, confidence gating, autonomous timing), the SE problems would remain intractable at scale.
temporalContext: The video was published on August 9, 2026. Resolve AI was founded in 2024 and launched its background agents feature in approximately June 2026, making this talk an early product presentation of a newly shipped capability. The talk occurs during a period of rapid MCP adoption (400M+ monthly SDK downloads as of mid-2026, with the stateless core spec released July 28, 2026). The broader context is the post-AI-coding-agent era where tools like Cursor and Copilot have accelerated code shipping velocity, creating the production operations gap that Resolve AI targets. Research was conducted on August 23, 2026.

concepts.name: Background agents
concepts.explanation: Always-on AI agents that autonomously handle operational work in production, defined by three principles: when they run (event-driven or scheduled), how they run (cloud sandbox with autonomous timing), and how they know what to do (learning system capturing environment knowledge).
concepts.importance: Central concept of the talk; defines a new class of AI agent distinct from interactive coding agents, focused on production operations rather than code generation.

concepts.name: Dynamic check plan generation via causal chain reasoning
concepts.explanation: Agents read actual release changes, identify affected services by following causal chains through production dependencies, and construct customized, release-specific monitoring plans rather than using hardcoded templates.
concepts.importance: Demonstrates how AI agents can reason about production system dependencies to generate context-aware monitoring — a key differentiator from static CI/CD rules.

concepts.name: Autonomous timing decisions
concepts.explanation: Agents decide when to recheck based on failure class — immediate retry, hourly check, or multi-day follow-up — rather than using fixed hardcoded intervals. An agent may autonomously decide to return in three days to verify deploy health.
concepts.importance: Shows agent reasoning extending to temporal decision-making, a capability that static monitoring systems cannot replicate.

concepts.name: Confidence-gated autonomous responses
concepts.explanation: Agents passively monitor channels and decide whether to respond publicly, ask for confirmation via DM, or stay silent based on self-assessed confidence. When uncertain, the agent DMs an engineer to confirm before replying publicly.
concepts.importance: Demonstrates a safety pattern for deploying autonomous AI agents in high-stakes communication environments where incorrect answers carry operational risk.

concepts.name: Learning system for environment knowledge
concepts.explanation: A system component that captures and retains knowledge about how a production environment operates, including service interactions and causal relationships, enabling agents to work effectively in evolving systems. The speaker states models alone are insufficient without this.
concepts.importance: Identified as essential for agent effectiveness; without it, agents cannot reason about production context, which is the hard half of operational tasks.

concepts.name: MCP-based composable agent integration
concepts.explanation: Using Model Context Protocol servers to expose agent capabilities for integration into existing internal agent harnesses, enabling bring-your-own-skills composition rather than requiring teams to adopt a monolithic platform.
concepts.importance: Connects the talk's agent architecture to the broader AI agent ecosystem and emerging standards, enabling interoperability with existing tooling.

concepts.name: Natural conversation-based agent configuration
concepts.explanation: Agents are set up through natural language conversation — the agent explores the environment, asks clarifying questions, and builds an understanding of what to monitor, rather than requiring configuration files or dashboards.
concepts.importance: Reduces setup friction for deploying autonomous agents in complex production environments, making agent deployment accessible through dialogue.

concepts.name: On-call workflows and incident management
concepts.explanation: The traditional practice of rotating engineers for production incident response, where lack of recent context on system changes creates friction, cognitive load, and slower resolution. The speaker describes on-call as a 'nightmare' because engineers go on call infrequently and may not understand all changes that have come in.
concepts.importance: Frames the operational pain point that background agents are designed to solve, motivating the entire talk.

concepts.name: CI/CD monitoring coverage gaps
concepts.explanation: CI/CD pipelines handle baseline checks well but leave gaps for feature flags and infrastructure changes that often ship with no monitoring at all, creating blind spots in production observability.
concepts.importance: Identifies the specific operational gaps that background agents fill beyond what traditional CI/CD already covers.

concepts.name: Production context as the hard problem
concepts.explanation: A task equals execution plus production context, where execution is the easy half. The real difficulty and cost lie in understanding the production environment, its service interactions, and causal relationships — not in executing the task itself.
concepts.importance: Core insight that reframes where engineering effort actually goes and what AI agents must understand to be useful in production.

concepts.name: Sandboxed cloud execution environment
concepts.explanation: Background agents run in the cloud inside a sandbox with their own file system, independent of local developer machines, enabling always-on operation even when laptops are closed.
concepts.importance: Defines the infrastructure requirement that makes always-on background agents feasible — a key engineering decision distinct from local coding agents.

concepts.name: Slack/Teams as primary interaction surface
concepts.explanation: Slack or MS Teams serves as the primary user-facing integration point for agents rather than a separate dashboard, meeting engineers where they already work in their daily flow.
concepts.importance: Defines the UX boundary for operational agent deployment in enterprise environments, reducing adoption friction.

sections.title: Background agent principles and four workloads
sections.summary: Smith defines three principles for background agents: when they run, how they run, and how they know what to do. He introduces four workloads: deployment monitoring, health checks, operational reports, and Slack first responder.

sections.title: Demos and closing takeaways
sections.summary: Smith demos deployment monitoring, on-call handoff reports, and passive Slack monitoring. He concludes that agents are set up through conversation, accessible via MCP servers, and cost lives in environment complexity.

organization.name: Resolve AI
organization.summary: Resolve AI is a privately held software company founded in 2024 and headquartered at 350 Rhode Island St, San Francisco, California, with an additional office in New York. The company builds AI agents for production operations, including on-call agents for alert triage, incident co-working agents, and background agents that run operational workflows on schedule or trigger. The product architecture comprises models, context, reasoning, actions, and a learning system that captures environment knowledge. Resolve AI's capabilities are accessible through MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, APIs, and Skills for composable integration into existing agent ecosystems. Customers include Coinbase, DoorDash, Expedia Group, Snowflake, Zscaler, MongoDB, Robinhood, Autodesk, Toast, Eventbrite, Pinecone, Guidewire, MSCI, and others. The company employs approximately 128 people across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. It claims up to 5x faster MTTR and 75% higher productivity. Resolve AI is distinct from similarly named companies including Resolve (resolve.io, IT/network operations, founded 2014), ResolveAI (resolveai.co, AI chatbots, Tel Aviv), and Rezolve AI (rezolve.ai, IT/HR/FinOps, Dublin CA).
organization.status: Active, privately held, approximately 128 employees, headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York. Raised $125M Series A at $1B valuation in February 2026. No parent company.

technologies.label: Background Agents
technologies.summary: Always-on autonomous AI agents that handle production operations without the on-call tax, defined by three principles: when they run (event-driven or scheduled), how they run (cloud sandbox with autonomous timing), and how they know what to do (learning system capturing environment knowledge). Four primary workloads are demonstrated: deployment monitoring with dynamic check plans that follow causal chains through production dependencies, scheduled health checks, operational reports and on-call handoffs, and passive Slack question response with confidence gating. Agent timing is autonomous — agents may decide to recheck in an hour or return in three days based on the failure class. Agents are configured through natural conversation rather than configuration files.
technologies.role: Central technology of the talk; defines a new class of AI agent distinct from interactive coding agents, focused on production operations rather than code generation. All four demonstrated workloads and architectural principles revolve around this concept.

technologies.label: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
technologies.summary: An open standard for connecting AI agents to external systems and tools, enabling composable agent design. The speaker states that all Resolve AI capabilities are accessible through MCP servers, allowing teams to bring their own skills and integrate into existing internal agent harnesses rather than adopting a monolithic platform. MCP has surpassed 400M monthly SDK downloads as of mid-2026 and moved to a stateless core architecture with the 2026-07-28 spec release.
technologies.role: Referenced as the composability mechanism enabling Resolve AI's integration into existing agent ecosystems, presented near the end of the talk as the deployment substrate for teams building their own agent harnesses.

technologies.label: Learning System for Environment Knowledge
technologies.summary: An architectural component that captures and retains knowledge about how a production environment operates, including service interactions and causal relationships. The speaker identifies this as essential because models alone are insufficient without deep understanding of the production environment. The core insight is that a task equals execution plus production context, where execution is the easy half and the cost of operational work lies in environment complexity.
technologies.role: Presented as the essential component that makes background agents effective. The speaker explicitly states models alone are insufficient without this learning system, framing production context as the hard problem that execution alone cannot solve.

technologies.label: Sandboxed Cloud Execution Environment
technologies.primary: Sandboxed cloud execution environment for agents
technologies.summary: The infrastructure architecture that makes always-on background agents feasible — agents run in the cloud inside a sandbox with their own file system, independent of developer machines. This enables agents to continue operating even when laptops are closed, and to interact with engineers through Slack or MS Teams rather than requiring a separate dashboard. The speaker describes this as 'always runs, it is in the cloud, if you close your laptop it is okay, runs inside of a sandbox so it has a file system underneath it.'
technologies.role: Presented as one of the three defining principles of background agents (how they run), explaining that agents are always on, cloud-resident, sandboxed with their own file system, and accessible through existing communication tools rather than requiring a separate dashboard.
